UNIDENTIFIED LOOT — 1.1.3

Minecraft 1.21.1 · NeoForge · Java 21 · TNK Edition

Dungeon rewards, expanded equipment pools and safer identification. Build themed loot pools, choose the equipment each dungeon can award, and keep earned rewards intact through identification, reforging and monthly rotations.

Rewards that belong to the dungeon

  • Dungeons can now choose specific weapons, armour and accessories instead of sending every equipment reward through a global item pool.
  • Equipment can arrive identified or unidentified. Unidentified dungeon rewards save the complete rolled item when the chest opens, so identification reveals that same equipment and its original stats.
  • Added reusable equipment presets for guaranteed enchantments, attribute bonuses, fixed affixes and optional random affixes. Bonuses can use fixed values or ranges, and random affixes can be restricted to a themed selection.
  • Preserved native armour, damage modifiers, enchantments and item components when applying dungeon bonuses.
  • Reforging dungeon equipment preserves its rarity and guaranteed bonuses, while rerolling the random affix portion from its saved tier and pool. Reforging materials must match the item's rarity.
  • Added optional spell-power and maximum-mana affixes for curated Iron's Spells armour rewards, without adding them to ordinary random equipment rolls.
  • Earned dungeon tokens and already-rolled payouts keep their saved results after monthly reward-table or preset changes.

Spiral Abyss integration

  • Added optional integration for the original Spiral Abyss 2.0.5 JAR, with one editable reward file per floor covering equipment, materials, food, potions and rare prizes.
  • Floor previews now show actual item variants, guaranteed bonuses, rarity odds and per-roll chances. Different versions of the same item remain separate, and potion previews retain their real potion effects.
  • The rare-reward journal uses the same custom reward definitions as the floor overview.
  • On configured custom floors, nine-star golden chests make one overall rare-reward check, followed by weighted prize selection. At most one identified rare prize is awarded across the eligible party, with the announcement retained on pickup.
  • Rare rewards support either a shared chest chance or scaling by eligible player count. Previews explain solo odds and the selected party-scaling rule.
  • Copper, iron and gold retain one, two and three normal rolls per eligible player. Existing floor challenges, experience, independent item bonuses, claims and arena mob-drop suppression are preserved.
  • Included a separate, opt-in six-floor example datapack with Arcane, Aether, Aquatic, Twilight, Infernal and End themes, shared presets and an editing guide. Its values are examples for pack authors to balance.

Expanded equipment compatibility

Added 63 equipment rules with explicit categories and tier ranges. Native item stats remain intact.

  • Vanilla Backport: copper equipment and copper spears use tiers 1–2, matching chainmail's loot band. Other spears follow their material's existing band; golden equipment remains excluded.
  • Deeper and Darker: resonarium and warden armour use tiers 6–7, above netherite's starting band, with equipment routed through Otherside pools.
  • The Beyond: brittle tools and swords use tiers 4–6; anchor leggings and pathfinder boots use 5–7, with End equipment routing.
  • Enderscape: drift leggings use tiers 5–7 and rubble shields use 3–5. End routing and native item-state preservation are supported.
  • Immersive Engineering: steel and Faraday armour use tiers 3–4, above iron. Ordinary steel tools and swords use 2–3.
  • Applied Energistics 2: certus-quartz, nether-quartz and fluix tools and swords use tiers 2–3, matching iron's loot band.
  • Archaion: the Echo Mace is exclusive to Last of Deepslate's tier-6 boss reward. Native Echo Charges and smithing-template drops are retained.
  • Filled missing Apotheosis categories for approved equipment, including added tools and the Echo Mace, so those items can receive affixes.

Native equipment and loot safeguards

  • Removed blank Iron's Jewelry rings and necklaces from TNK identification and random Apotheosis pools. Properly generated jewellery retains its native pattern and material data.
  • Removed obsolete Epic Fight: Nightfall presets and stale equipment entries from migrated configurations.
  • Kept Vinery, Brewery and HerbalBrews clothing; Hybrid Aquatic equipment; Jaden's Nether Expansion and Wildernature equipment; and Supplementaries slingshots/quivers out of generated TNK equipment pools. Native crafting, item use and stored contents remain available.
  • Deeper and Darker's staff and soul elytra, The Beyond's Ring Remembrance, powered/modular utility equipment and Archaion's Echo's Grace retain native handling instead of entering ordinary TNK equipment rolls.
  • Corrected NPC identification for saved dungeon rewards that have no matching global item pool. Saved results retain their original equipment and stats.
  • Ordinary resource rewards retain normal stacking, and explicitly sealed rewards are preserved during normal chest processing and hostile loot filtering.

Pack configuration and previews

  • Added tnkloot:dungeon_reward for editable weighted reward definitions, plus tnkloot:seal_reward for vanilla loot tables with an explicit equipment tier, source level and rarity. Sealing supports actual selected equipment, optional presets and identified delivery, while retaining the earlier generic-token behaviour.
  • Custom dungeon rewards use their authored floor strength; identification does not reroll them against a later owner's progression cap.
  • Added Enderscape/The Beyond equipment routing and an Otherside route. Removed stale BetterEnd/BetterNether namespace references when those mods are absent, while retaining custom route settings.
  • Configuration migration creates backups and preserves existing weights, disabled-item choices and custom dimension settings. Approved tier changes apply once, leaving later manual edits intact.
  • Invalid dungeon definitions are rejected before replacing the working reward catalog.
  • Added normal-reward percentages and clearer bonus/party information to Spiral previews, with compact text and room for the tooltip frame at larger GUI scales.
  • Retained the approved blue/copper CleanLook interface, brown equipment slots, artwork, fonts, models and Ponder resources.

Installation notes

  • Update both client and server to 1.1.3. Requires TNK Progression 1.1.0+ and the existing required companion mods. Optional integrations remain optional.
  • For custom Spiral floors, install the separate example datapack in world/datapacks. Use the original Spiral Abyss 2.0.5 JAR. Restart after replacing Loot; apply later datapack edits with /reload between attempts, as Spiral cancels active attempts on reload.
  • Enderscape server setup: the tested Enderscape 1.0.9 also needs YACL installed on the server. Its config classes load there despite its client-only dependency metadata. This does not add a hard YACL dependency to Unidentified Loot.
  • The jewellery safeguard prevents new blank rewards; it does not automatically repair already-broken jewellery in inventories.

Validation: 27 automated tests passed, alongside focused checks using the actual optional mods, all 63 approved equipment entries, native End item-state preservation and 900 golden-chest payouts. The complete 307-mod pack has not been run together.
